::: {#def-p-value}
#### p-value

Given a [test statistic](#def-test-statistic) $T$
whose observed value is $t$,
the **p-value** is the probability
that $T$ is at least as extreme as the value observed,
computed with the data distributed as the null hypothesis specifies:

$$p \eqdef \Pr_{H_0}(T \ge t)$$

If the null hypothesis allows more than one distribution
(a *composite* null hypothesis, such as $H_0: \mean_1 = \mean_0$ with unknown variances),
the p-value is the largest such probability over those distributions,
or an approximation to it.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#rem-p-value-not-posterior}
#### A p-value is not the probability that the null hypothesis is true

A p-value is computed assuming $H_0$ is true,
so it is not the probability that $H_0$ is true given the data.
:::
